requirements.statement: A plan can mark objectives as 'must pass': the true core functionality of the feature
The must-pass marking is carried into the success definition, so verification knows which criteria are must-pass
Verification cannot end 'satisfied' unless every must-pass criterion is 'met', whatever the coverage-floor percentage
A must-pass criterion that is 'not_verifiable' (or 'not_met', or 'unbuilt') blocks 'satisfied' exactly as a missing one would
When verification is blocked by must-pass criteria, the report and the readout name each blocking criterion, so the owner sees which core item was not proven
Every must-pass objective is covered by at least one must-pass criterion; a must-pass objective with no criterion is reported, not silently dropped
The coverage floor still applies, separately, over all criteria
A plan that marks no objective must-pass keeps today's verification behaviour, and the readout says that none was declared
